starting_principles: Newton's Second Law for charge carriers under an electric field: $\vec{F} = q \vec{E} = m \vec{a}$
Classical Drude momentum relaxation time hypothesis: average directed velocity gained between random collisions is $\vec{v}_d = \vec{a}\tau$
Definition of electric current as charge flux: $I = \frac{dq}{dt}$
assumptions: Free electron gas model in a uniform, isotropic metallic conductor
Randomizing collisions with lattice ions characterized by an average momentum relaxation time $\tau$
Isotropic thermal velocity distribution with zero net thermal drift velocity $\langle \vec{v}_{\text{thermal}} \rangle = \vec{0}$
Uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ and uniform cross-sectional area $A$ along the conductor

ordered_steps.description: Determine the acceleration of a conduction electron of mass $m$ and charge $-e$ in an applied electric field $\vec{E}$.
ordered_steps.operation: Apply Newton's second law $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$ and isolate $\vec{a}$
assumptions_applied: Classical particle dynamics for conduction electrons
Homogeneous electric field throughout the conductor cross-section

ordered_steps.description: Calculate the ensemble-averaged drift velocity $\vec{v}_d$ accumulated over mean relaxation time $\tau$.
ordered_steps.operation: Take the statistical ensemble average with $\langle \vec{v}_{\text{thermal}} \rangle = \vec{0}$ and average collision interval $\langle t \rangle = \tau$
assumptions_applied: Isotropic random thermal velocity distribution with zero mean

ordered_steps.description: Relate drift speed magnitude $v_d$ to electric field magnitude $E$ using electron mobility $\mu$.
ordered_steps.operation: Define electron mobility $\mu = \frac{e\tau}{m}$ as drift speed per unit field

ordered_steps.description: Calculate the total mobile charge $\Delta q$ crossing a transverse cross-sectional area $A$ in time $\Delta t$.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute cylinder volume $\Delta V_{\text{cyl}} = A \Delta x = A (v_d \Delta t)$ swept by drifting carriers
ordered_steps.result_equation: $\Delta q = n e A v_d \Delta t$

ordered_steps.description: Formulate macroscopic electric current $I$ as the time rate of charge transport.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $\Delta q = n e A v_d \Delta t$ and take the derivative

ordered_steps.description: Express current density vector $\vec{J}$ and derive microscopic Ohm's law.
assumptions_applied: Linear constitutive relation between current density and electric field

applicability_conditions: Valid for ohmic metallic conductors in the regime $v_d \ll v_{\text{thermal}}$
Constant temperature maintaining invariant electron relaxation time $\tau$
Uniform carrier concentration and cross-sectional area
